root_cause: The branch-resolution/mispredict path is incomplete: when a conditional branch predicted taken actually resolves not-taken, the core does not redirect to the fall-through path and flush the predicted-target fetch. The 2-instruction 64-iteration loops therefore never exit; x1 keeps counting iterations (0x1f1d=7965) and retired count scales as ~2*x1 (15931). The same missing not-taken resolve/mispredict event explains the missing dbg_bp_resolve evidence and the repeated 63 mispredicts. ECALL is never reached, so all halt waits time out; this is a control-transfer recovery bug, not a halt-commit or ready/valid handshake bug.
repair_constraints: Never rename modules, files, or ports; preserve every interface in the plan contract.
Keep PC priority: reset > redirect on control transfer > ECALL halt freeze > load-use pause > PC+4.

Every valid control transfer, including a conditional branch that resolves not-taken, must produce exactly one single-cycle bp_resolve event; bp_mispredict must be asserted in the same cycle only when the predicted next PC differs from the actual next PC.
A predicted-taken but actually-not-taken branch must redirect the front end to pc+4 and flush all predicted-path instructions; predicted-target requests must not survive.
Preserve the branch-predictor training update from real resolve state; do not fabricate debug events with counters or PC patterns.

If the I-cache response epoch guard is added or repaired, latch inflight_epoch when the request is accepted and discard a response whose epoch does not match flush_epoch; do not advance PC or write IF/ID on a discarded response, and re-issue the fetch.
Preserve ECALL propagation ID→EX→MEM→WB and the halt/retire timing: one retire event per committed instruction, halted/exit_code committed on the following edge, outputs stable after halted.
Preserve external handshake behavior: hold valid/address until ready and never abort an in-flight cache request.
evidence: cache_instruction_reuse and predictor_training both report x1 expected 0x40 got 0x1f1d; predictor_training reports retired count expected 132 got 15931 and 63 mispredicts. 0x1f1d = 7965 and 15931 ≈ 2*7965+1, exactly matching a runaway 2-instruction loop counter. Multiple tests freeze at different loop PCs (0x1c, 0x2c, 0x3c, 0xdc) while x1 and retired count keep advancing; predictor_training also reports missing branch-resolution evidence.
